properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Cleveland County in the piedmont of North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 830 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots. Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible. A small
culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 224 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a several rounds of
torrential rainfall are moving through Cleveland County, with
additional cells of moderate rainfall moving into the county from
the south.  This rainfall is occurring on top of saturated soils
due to a prolonged period of light to moderate showers that have
occurred over the county since yesterday morning.  Widespread,
storm-total rainfall of the 1.5-3.5 inches fell yesterday, with
the highest totals near the Rutherford County line.  The rainfall
has accumulated steadily, allowing soils to slowly saturate and
runoff to slowly increase, resulting in steady rises in small
streams. However, this current period of torrential rainfall may
cause more rapid rises to develop, especially in the city of
Shelby, along Sandy Run near Mooresboro Rd, and along Ashworth
Creek near McCraw Rd.  Isolated out-of-bank conditions impacting
low-lying areas adjacent to streams are likely to develop over
the next 1-3 hours.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop
between 4am and 9am this morning.  These showers and storms will
be very efficient at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are
saturated and streams are swollen. Therefore, additional heavy
rain may quickly create new areas of flooding and cause previous
areas of flooding to redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood
Warnings may be issued tonight.  Caution is advised near any
stream or other vulnerable area.  Seek higher ground immediately
if heavy rain develops.  Please have a plan in place should flash
flooding develop and do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all
evacuation orders from Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Shelby, Kings Mountain, Boiling Springs NC, Belwood, Grover,

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 11:16PM EDT until October 11 at 5:15AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
FFWGSP

The National Weather Service in Greenville-Spartanburg has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Henderson County in western North Carolina...
Polk County in western North Carolina...
Eastern Transylvania County in western North Carolina...

* Until 515 AM EDT.

* At 1116 PM EDT, Earlier today, a prolonged period of steady
rainfall produced 3-6 inches across eastern Transylvania,
Henderson, and Polk counties, saturating area soils and causing
scattered areas of nuisance flooding.  Doppler radar shows several
rounds of torrential rainfall has moved through the area from the
south, capable of producing 2-3 inches of rainfall on top of
saturated soils.  This rainfall will exacerbate areas of ongoing
nuisance flooding and cause new areas of Minor flooding to develop.

* Areas of greatest concern include along the Little River from Cedar
Mountain to Penrose; the Davidson River near Pisgah Forest; the
French Broad River from Brevard to Mills River; Mud Creek from Crab
Creek to Hendersonville to Mountain Home; White Oak Creek from Mill
Spring to Green Creek; and Boylston Creek near Forge Mountain.

* Additional areas of Minor Flooding are expected to develop over the
next 1-3 hours.  Please obey all barricades and heed all evacuation
orders from local Emergency Management officials.  Only a few
inches of water can strand your vehicle and only 6 inches of water
can sweep your vehicle away.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Expect flash flooding of low-lying areas near streams,
including parks, trails, low-water crossings, boat- access
areas, and campgrounds.  Significant flooding of
poor-drainage areas are likely, impacting travel.
Low-lying roadways are likely to be flooded, requiring
barricades.   An isolated landslide or two cannot be ruled
out.

* Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Hendersonville, Brevard, Columbus, Mills River, Fletcher, Flat
Rock, Etowah, Mountain Home, Laurel Park and Tryon.
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

The additional heavy rain will increase the risk of landslides and
debris flows, especially in areas where landslides have occurred in
the past. Be especially alert if you live near a stream, particularly
at the base of a mountain or in a cove. Watch for signs that a
landslide may be imminent, including loose-moving soil and rocks or a
sudden increase in streamflow. Stay indoors and do NOT go outside to
investigate. Escape vertically inside your home by moving upstairs or
getting on top of counters to avoid being swept away.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southwestern Avery County in western North Carolina...
Southeastern Mitchell County in western North Carolina...
Southeastern Yancey County in western North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 500 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible. A
few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.

- At 1102 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 2 and 6 inches of rain have
fallen along the ridges of the southern parts of Yancey, Mitchell
and Avery counties.

develop on North Toe River and South Toe River, as well.

develop over the next few hours and the threat will persist
through the early morning hours on Sunday. These showers and
storms will be very efficient at producing heavy rainfall. Soils
are saturated and streams are swollen. Therefore, additional
heavy rain may quickly create new areas of flooding and cause
previous areas of flooding to redevelop.  As a result, Flash
Flood Warnings may be issued tonight. Caution is advised near any
stream or other vulnerable area. Seek higher ground immediately
if heavy rain develops. Please have a plan in place should flash
flooding develop and do not hesitate to act. Please heed all
evacuation orders from Emergency Management officials.

Spruce Pine, B.R. Parkway-Little Switzerland To Linville, B.R.
Parkway-Craggy To Little Switzerland, Mount Mitchell State Park,

properties.title: Tropical Storm Watch issued October 10 at 8:05PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* LOCATIONS AFFECTED
- Oceanside
- Carlsbad
- Chula Vista
- San Diego

* WIND
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind
- Peak Wind Forecast: 10-20 mph with gusts to 30 mph

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 39
to 57 mph
- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Plan for hazardous wind of equivalent tropical storm
force.
- PREPARE: Efforts to protect property should now be
underway. Prepare for limited wind damage.
- ACT: Act now to complete preparations before the wind
becomes hazardous.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees
are shallow rooted, especially in coastal and valley
locations that don't typically experience strong winds.
Some fences and roadway signs blown over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within
urban or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving
conditions on bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* STORM SURGE
- While true storm surge is unlikely, significant coastal flooding
and beach erosion from high tides near 7.5 feet, high surf, and
increased onshore winds expected.

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Little to no storm
surge flooding
- PLAN: Coastal flooding, rough surf, coastal erosion, and
life-threatening rip currents are possible.
- PREPARE: Do not make plans to go to the beach. Take necessary
actions to protect flood prone property.
- ACT: Follow the instructions of local officials. Monitor
forecasts.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant coastal flooding and beach erosion
possible. Dangerous swimming conditions due to high surf and
strong rip currents.

* FLOODING RAIN
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Flood Watch is in effect
- Peak Rainfall Amounts: Additional around 1 inch

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for major
flooding rain
- The flooding rain threat has remained nearly steady from
the previous assessment.
- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for
major flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues are
likely.
- PREPARE: Strongly consider protective actions, especially
if you are in an area vulnerable to flooding.
- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings. Failure to take
action will likely result in serious injury or loss of life.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Extensive
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, canals, arroyos,
and ditches may become dangerous rivers. In mountain areas,
destructive runoff may run quickly down valleys while
increasing susceptibility to rockslides and mudslides.
Flood control systems and barriers may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or
washed away. Many places where flood waters may cover
escape routes. Streets and parking lots become rivers of
moving water with underpasses submerged. Driving conditions
become dangerous. Many road and bridge closures with some
weakened or washed out.

* TORNADO
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:
- Situation is unfavorable for tornadoes

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Tornadoes not expected
- The tornado threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Tornadoes are not expected. Showers and thunderstorms
with gusty winds may still occur.
- PREPARE: Little to no preparations needed to protect
against tornadoes at this time. Keep informed of the latest
tornado situation.
- ACT: Listen for changes in the forecast.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Little to None
- Little to no potential impacts from tornadoes.

* FOR MORE INFORMATION:
- sdcountyemergency.com

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 8:19PM EDT until October 11 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Spartanburg County in upstate South Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 800 AM EDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to streams
and other poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks,
greenways, boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and
parking lots.  Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.
A few flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A
small culvert washout or two is possible.


* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 803 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated a thunderstorm producing
torrential rainfall is quickly moving from south to north across
the county.  This torrential rainfall is occurring on top of
saturated soils due to a prolonged period of light to moderate
showers that have occurred over the county since this morning.
Widespread, storm-total rainfall of the 2.5-3.5 inches have
fallen over the past 12 hours. The rainfall has accumulated
steadily, allowing soils to slowly saturate and runoff to slowly
increase, resulting in steady rises in the small streams.
However, this brief period of torrential rainfall is causing more
rapid rises to develop, including along Lawsons Fork Creek from
Inman to Spartanburg, the South Pacolet River near Campobello,
the North Tyger River near Wellford and Lyman, and small
tributaries to these rivers including Jordan Creek, Motlow Creek,
and Meadow Creek.  Isolated out-of-bank conditions are likely to
develop over the next 1-3 hours.

Glendale Fire Department is reporting nuisance flooding along
Country Club Rd near Church St.  Please obey all barricades and
avoid flooded roadways.  Only a few inches of water can strand
your vehicle.

- Additional rounds of showers and thunderstorms may develop over
the next few hours and the threat will persist through the early
morning hours on Sunday.  These showers and storms will be very
efficient at producing heavy rainfall.  Soils are saturated and
streams are swollen. Therefore, additional heavy rain may quickly
create new areas of flooding and cause previous areas of flooding
to redevelop.  As a result, Flash Flood Warnings may be issued
tonight.  Caution is advised near any stream or other vulnerable
area.  Seek higher ground immediately if heavy rain develops.
Please have a plan in place   should flash flooding develop and
do not hesitate to act.  Please heed all evacuation orders from
Emergency Management officials.

- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Spartanburg, Greer, Boiling Springs SC, Woodruff, Duncan, Lyman,
Pacolet, Landrum, Cowpens and Wellford.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

Pigeon River At above Old River Rd (NC 215), 1 SW Canton affecting
Haywood County.

.Tropical rainfall will continue to overspread the mountains through
tonight and become heavier. Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is
expected, with isolated higher amounts possible across the upper
Pigeon River watershed upstream of Canton.  The highest totals will
occur along the Pisgah ridge and in the Shining Rock and Middle Prong

low-lying areas adjacent to the Pigeon River, including farmland,
woodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways, parks, and other
